Statement: When I schedule a customer callback, I want the system to track and enforce the deadline so callbacks happen on time.
Evidence: Cases get stuck in 'pending callback' status indefinitely because the callback date is never enforced.
Relevance: Follow-ups are not missed and repayments are enforced more vigorously.

Statement: When I record customer communication about payment, I want to distinguish between payment promises and confirmed payments so there's no confusion about what's actually owed.
Evidence: The current system treats payment promises the same as payment confirmations, which creates confusion.
Relevance: There is a clear record about repayment the avoid any future confusion.

Statement: When I prepare to contact a customer, I want to see how many times they've been contacted this month so I don't duplicate outreach.
Evidence: I cannot tell which customers have already been contacted this month without manually checking three different sheets
Relevance: Prevents duplicate effort and breach of contact regulations.

Statement: When I review a case's history, I want to understand why it changed status so I can make informed decisions.
Evidence: Status updates do not capture why a case changed state, only that it did.
Relevance: Provides insight to the case and helps find the best resolution between the bank and the customer.

Statement: When I manage my workload, I want straightforward cases to be prioritized appropriately so they're resolved quickly.
Evidence: Straightforward cases get delayed because they are queued behind complex ones with no priority logic.
Relevance: Improves workflows, more time for complex cases.

Statement: When I report on case activity, I want consistent status definitions across the team so reporting is accurate and actionable.
Evidence: Different representatives use different status codes, which makes reporting meaningless.
Relevance: No confusions between the teams on the meaning of codes.
